issues: Material clarity is too weak: primary, surface, or finish is missing or vague.
Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Lock material.primary, material.surface, and material.finish to a specific engineered matte ceramic read.
Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: To render a simple geometric test of a white ceramic sphere on a black background, prioritizing a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read within a material-study scope.

must_have: clear, readable contour of a manufactured sphere
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.background: solid black background, devoid of detail

constraints: even illumination across the sphere's surface
lighting designed to highlight material properties
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: abstract composition leading to subject loss
material drift towards forbidden reads (e.g., plaster, glossy plastic)
failure to achieve a clean matte technical ceramic read
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: lock the object read to a singular, manufactured ceramic sphere
prevent abstract drift or atmospheric dominance
strictly suppress all forbidden material reads
maintain material-only scope without compromising object readability
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: immediate and unambiguous read of a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material
clear evidence of a dry, dense, engineered manufactured object
the ceramic sphere is the sole, clearly defined subject
no visual cues suggesting plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Generate a clear, ENTITY_MEDIUM shot of a single, manufactured ceramic sphere. The primary focus is on achieving a clean, matte B4C technical ceramic material read, strictly avoiding any forbidden material interpretations or abstract compositional drift. The background must be solid black, and lighting should be even to highlight the material's properties.
